transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

This is a very common issue with Hotpoint (and many other brands) tumble dryers. Since you can hear the motor running but the drum isn't turning, the problem is almost certainly a broken drive belt or a failed idler pulley.

Here’s how to diagnose and fix it safely:

### ⚠️ Safety First
1. Unplug the dryer from the wall before doing anything.
2. If your dryer has a gas supply, turn off the gas valve as well (though most Hotpoint drum issues are electric/mechanical).

---

### Most Likely Cause: Broken Drive Belt
The belt connects the motor to the drum. Over time, it stretches, wears out, or snaps. When it breaks, the motor runs but nothing turns the drum.

#### How to Check:
1. Access the back panel: Remove the screws holding the rear panel of the dryer and take it off. (Some models require removing the top panel instead—check your manual.)
2. Locate the belt: You’ll see a black rubber belt wrapped around the drum, a motor pulley, and an idler pulley (a small wheel that keeps tension on the belt).
3. Inspect the belt:
• Is it snapped in two? → Replace the belt.
• Is it loose or slipped off the pulleys? → It may have jumped off due to a broken idler pulley. Try re-routing it (see below).
• Does it look frayed, cracked, or glazed? → Replace the belt.

#### If the Belt Looks Intact:
Check the idler pulley (the tensioner wheel). It should spin freely and quietly. If it’s seized, noisy, or doesn’t spin, replace it. A stuck idler pulley can cause the belt to snap or slip off.

---

### Less Common Causes:
1. Motor Capacitor Failure:
• The capacitor helps start the motor. If it fails, the motor may hum but not have enough torque to turn the drum (especially if clothes are heavy).
• Test: With the dryer unplugged, check for a bulging or leaking capacitor near the motor. Replace if damaged.

2. Motor Fan Blade Broken:
• Some motors use a fan blade on the end to help pull air and assist rotation. If it’s broken off, the motor may struggle to turn the drum.

3. Drum Rollers/Wheels Worn Out (if your model has them):
• Older Hotpoint models have rollers at the back of the drum. If these are seized or worn, the drum won’t turn easily. Spin the drum by hand—if it’s stiff or gritty, replace the rollers.

---

### Step-by-Step Fix for Belt Replacement:
1. Buy a replacement belt specific to your Hotpoint model (find the model number on the door frame or inside the door seal).
2. Remove the old belt: Note how it’s routed around the drum, motor pulley, and idler pulley. Take a photo for reference.
3. Install the new belt:
• Loop it around the drum first.
• Then stretch it over the motor pulley and idler pulley. You may need to pull the motor away slightly or press down on the idler arm to create slack.
4. Reassemble the panels.
5. Test: Plug in the dryer and run a short cycle without clothes to ensure the drum turns smoothly.

---

### When to Call a Professional:
• If you’re uncomfortable opening the dryer.
• If the belt is intact but the motor still doesn’t turn (could be a faulty motor or control board).
• If you hear grinding noises (suggests internal gear or bearing failure).

Let me know your exact Hotpoint model number if you need help finding parts!

Based on your description—specifically that the drum spins easily by hand and you found a black rubbery strip—this confirms the issue beyond doubt:

### 🔧 The Problem: Broken Drive Belt
The "rubbery strip" is your drive belt. It has snapped, which is why the motor runs (you hear it) but the drum doesn’t turn. The fact that the drum spins freely by hand means there’s no mechanical blockage (like a foreign object jammed in the drum), which is good news.

---

### ✅ Solution: Replace the Drive Belt
You’ll need to buy a replacement belt for your Hotpoint dryer. Since the model number is worn, here’s how to find the correct part:

#### 1. Identify Your Exact Model
Look for other labels on your dryer:
• Inside the door frame (on the metal rim).
• On the top edge of the front panel (under the lint filter housing).
• On the back near the power cord entry.
• The model usually starts with "TVHM8..." followed by 3–4 more characters (e.g., TVHM8910N, TVHM8920W, etc.).

If you can’t find it, tell me any other numbers on the sticker (like a serial number or power rating), and I’ll help you narrow it down. Alternatively, you can search for "Hotpoint TVHM8 belt" online—many belts are universal across similar models.

#### 2. Parts You’ll Likely Need
• Drive Belt: Usually costs £10–£20.
• Idler Pulley (Tensioner Wheel): It’s highly recommended to replace this at the same time, as it wears out alongside the belt and can cause the new belt to break prematurely. Cost: ~£5–£10.

#### 3. How to Replace the Belt (Step-by-Step)
Since you’ve already removed the back panel, here’s what to do next:

Tools Needed:
• Screwdriver (Phillips head).
• Pliers (optional, for stretching the belt).
• New belt and idler pulley.

Steps:
1. Remove the Top Panel:
• Locate two screws at the back of the top panel (near where you removed the back panel).
• Remove these screws and slide the top panel forward slightly to release it from the front clips, then lift it off. This gives you access to the drum and motor.

2. Locate the Motor and Idler Pulley:
• The motor is usually at the bottom rear of the dryer.
• The idler pulley is a small wheel mounted on a spring-loaded arm that keeps tension on the belt.

3. Remove the Old Belt:
• Note how the old belt was routed around the drum, motor pulley, and idler pulley (take a photo if possible).
• Release the tension by pushing the idler pulley arm toward the motor to slacken the belt, then slip the belt off.

4. Replace the Idler Pulley (Recommended):
• Unscrew the old idler pulley and replace it with the new one. Ensure it spins freely.

5. Fit the New Belt:
• Loop the new belt around the drum first.
• Then, route it around the motor pulley and over the idler pulley.
• Push the idler pulley arm toward the motor to create slack, then stretch the belt onto the final pulley section.
• Ensure the belt is seated correctly in all grooves.

6. Reassemble:
• Replace the top panel (slide it back into place and secure with screws).
• Reattach the back panel if you removed it fully.
• Plug in the dryer and test.

---

### 💡 Pro Tip:
• When fitting the new belt, make sure it’s not twisted. It should lie flat against all pulleys.
• If your dryer has a drum support roller (a wheel at the back of the drum that supports its weight), check if it spins freely. If it’s seized, replace it too, as it can cause premature belt wear.
